# Native callback parameters in an actual invocation

Witness's allocation gate can observe a callback value passed to a source
helper, but the context-free callee query intentionally cannot resolve the
helper's callable parameter. The native call and its already-borrowed caller
frame supply the missing agreement. Primitive owns that observation; Witness
continues to own eligibility, universal-path and benchmark policy.

Material assumptions, evidence and consequences:

- A callback parameter identifies its runtime function without caller context:
  VERIFIED false. The paired query leaves the context-free result absent and
  requires two actual calls to the same helper to return their distinct source
  arguments. The initial forwarding implementation failed this assertion.
- A callback capturing a different runner can establish authority for the
  selected runner: VERIFIED false. The native selected/other capture pair
  distinguishes the original Go free variables and actual argument slots.
- Native type conversions, repeated helper bindings, nil, a root's unknown
  parameter and merged callable values preserve those distinctions: VERIFIED
  for the 48-case authored source partition. This is not exhaustion of Go.
- A source loan proves unconditional runtime execution: UNVERIFIED and not
  claimed. Conditional source calls remain possible invocations; the consumer
  must establish its own before-return and timing agreement.
- An imported implementation invokes a callback stored in its request:
  UNVERIFIED by this capability. Imported bodies remain absent. This slice
  does not introduce a callback execution catalog or infer a provider contract.
- Working memory grows with argument width: VERIFIED false for the measured
  query at 32 and 8,193 extra arguments, excluding Go's whole-unit compiler
  construction. The native query allocates zero times at both widths. Active
  borrowed ancestry and native compiler storage are separately owned; constant
  memory in arbitrary call depth is not claimed.

Fundamental facts: Go owns function parameters, actual call argument ordering,
callable representation changes and closure bindings. A private invocation
frame already identifies the actual caller. Following that frame's exact native
argument slot needs neither a second alias table nor an input-size quota.

The shared function projector now accepts the existing invocation loan.
Context-free callers pass no invocation and retain their absence semantics.
The contextual query authenticates the current call and each actual parent
binding, then lends the original source function/value. Contextual capture
binding compares against the selected argument in the actual closure's native
ancestor. No call graph, copied environment or function population is retained.

Retain the real RED forwarding-query failure and the failed-only correction;
the selected-capture RED and failed-only correction; all source partitions;
native identity/custody, malformed-argument and signature-cause refusals;
cancellation with its original cause; stopped-prefix and consumer-panic proof;
and exact zero-allocation width samples. The first hostile attempt mutated a
borrowed outer iterator before stopping it and panicked in the fixture. Keep
that attempt separate from production proof and recover only failed/uncompleted
leaves. A stopped parent loan precedes every destructive native mutation.

Deliberate controls must compile and fail assertions: incorrectly admit an
unselected capture, and allocate an argument-sized copy. Restore source before
the failed-only baseline checks. Run only the affected GoToolchain scope;
reuse unchanged proof. Final tools precede serial three-second fuzz and benchmark
runs, with source digests, commands, native output and receipts retained in the
HDD warehouse. The owner has temporarily required native Mac execution and
prohibited Anvil calls. No author-issued independent acceptance is claimed.
